top_choice_rationale: P001 is the only award on the slate and I prefer it to no award on the science. The magic-wavelength lattice is one simple, fully understood mechanism: both clock levels are shifted equally, so many atoms are trapped in the Lamb-Dicke regime without Doppler or recoil shifts, and the remaining systematics have been modelled. Independent laboratories reproduce fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, and the clocks resolve gravitational redshift across millimetres. The allocation to Katori (concept and first strontium demonstrations) and Ye (accuracy, stability and many-atom control) matches the two halves of the achievement, and the citation is narrow enough to stay distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. Residual reservations are that this is a measurement capability whose fundamental-physics payoffs are still prospective, and that credit for Takamoto, Lemonde and the ion-clock groups lies outside the pair, but they do not outweigh the established results.
